threads.body: Creating `Content(parts=[])` unconditionally turns a candidate whose chunks all have `content=None` (for example, a blocked response) into an empty output message. `to_output_messages()` skips contentless candidates, so this changes existing behavior and differs from non-streamed responses. Leave merged content unset until a chunk supplies content, and add a regression test confirming that an entirely contentless candidate produces no output message in both streaming variants.

+def _merge_streamed_candidates(candidates: list[Candidate]) -> list[Candidate]:
+    """Merge the per-chunk candidates of a stream into one candidate per index.
+
+    Each streamed chunk carries a fragment of the response; adjacent text
+    fragments of the same kind are joined so a streamed response is reported
+    like the equivalent non-streamed one.
+    """
+    merged: dict[int, Candidate] = {}
+    for candidate in candidates:
+        index = candidate.index or 0
+        target = merged.get(index)
+        if target is None:
+            target = merged[index] = Candidate(
+                index=candidate.index, content=Content(parts=[])
+            )
+        if candidate.finish_reason is not None:
+            target.finish_reason = candidate.finish_reason
+        if not candidate.content:
+            continue
+        if candidate.content.role:
+            target.content.role = candidate.content.role

threads.body:
This will return the items in the order they were received, no necessarily their index order. We could do something like this to guarantee the order:

```suggestion
    return [merged[index] for index in sorted(merged)]
```
